title: A hymn in Prabhati
hook: Kabir's hymn in Prabhati starts with one light and ends with a question: so who is good, and who is bad?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Raga Prabhati, the dawn raga, where Guru Nanak calls the Name an ornament. Your line was dawn. What did you put on first this morning? Day one thousand one hundred twenty-five.

So who is good, and who is bad? It's a question people ask about strangers on the news, about the neighbors, about the driver who just cut in. It's usually asked with an answer already waiting. In the Prabhati section of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Bhagat Kabir asks it too, in a hymn the Gurus placed among their own. But he asks it at the end of a sentence that begins with light. By the time the question arrives, a ready answer may not fit. Today: Kabir's hymn of the one light.
screen: `SO WHO IS GOOD, AND WHO IS BAD?` → `KABIR, IN PRABHATI.` → `A QUESTION THAT BEGINS WITH LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the opening, in paraphrase. First, God brought forth the light, and from that power came all people. From one light the whole world sprang up. So who is good, and who is bad? Kabir uses the name Allah here, and the word noor for light; in other hymns he calls the One Ram, among other names. Then the center line, the Rahao. In paraphrase: people, don't wander lost in doubt. The Creator is in the creation, and the creation is in the Creator, filling every place. Then Kabir picks up a pot. The clay is one, he says; the Maker shaped it in many ways. There's no fault in the clay pots, and no fault in the potter. The One is in everything, and all of it happens by the Maker's doing. Whoever recognizes the Maker's will, the hukam, knows the One. The hymn closes with Kabir himself: the Guru gave him something sweet, his fear went, and he sees the Pure One everywhere. Now set that hymn at daybreak, where tradition sings Prabhati. Dawn light doesn't pick. It reaches the dome of the gurdwara and the alley behind it, the person you love and the person you can't stand. Before the sun is high, everything is lit the same way, from one source. That's the picture Kabir puts in front of the question. If everyone is clay from one pit, shaped by one hand, lit by one light, then good and bad stop being two kinds of people. The hymn doesn't say no one does wrong. It says no one is made of different stuff. Your line: light at dawn.
screen: `FROM ONE LIGHT, THE WHOLE WORLD.` · `THE CREATOR IN THE CREATION.` · `ONE CLAY, MANY POTS.` · `DAWN LIGHT DOESN'T PICK.` · then, large: `LIGHT AT DAWN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen to one Prabhati shabad, and let the light fall evenly. If you can, play Kabir's hymn of the one light, or another shabad sung in Prabhati. If not, sit in the quiet. Bring to mind one person you love. Let the breath go out toward them. Then one person you hardly know: whoever delivered your last parcel, a voice on a help line. Same breath. Then, gently, someone you find hard. You don't have to feel anything special. Just let the same breath, the same light, reach all three, the way morning reaches every street. If you pray, you can remember the one light Kabir names. If you don't, simply notice the three faces side by side. The bell holds the time.
A hymn in Prabhati. Kabir's song that from one light the whole world sprang up, one clay shaped into many pots, so who is good, and who is bad? Today's word.

Your line: light at dawn. Once today, when you catch yourself sorting someone into good or bad, think of two pots from the same clay, and ask Kabir's question. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: Kabir's hymn of the one light is sung in kirtan in Raga Prabhati and is sometimes quoted when Sikhs speak of the equality of all people.

fork.setup: you're Kabir. you've just sung that the whole world sprang from one light. what comes next in your line?
options: so the good must be rewarded.
so who is good, and who is bad?
so stay away from the bad.
fork.reveal: the hymn asks the question right after the light: if all came from one light, who is good, and who is bad?

original.note: light: Kabir's word in Prabhati for the one light the world sprang from.

trapdoor: what you thought: some people are good, and some are bad, and that's that.
what it means: Kabir says all came from one light and one clay, so the line between kinds of people falls away.
what a scholar hears: Kabir turns Creator and creation around each other in the Rahao: the Creator in the creation, the creation in the Creator.

sources.ref: Prabhati, Bani Bhagat Kabir, 'Aval Allah noor upaia', Ang 1349
